newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: New Agrobanka owner to hold 51 pct stake.
newsitem.headline: New Agrobanka owner to hold 51 pct stake.

text.p: A new strategic investor to be chosen to manage the troubled Czech bank Agrobanka a.s. will hold a 51 percent stake, the central bank's administrator of Agrobanka told a news conference on Thursday.
"The new majority investor will have a 51 percent stake," the administrator, Jiri Klumpar, told a news conference.

He said that the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) "had confirmed an interest" in taking a stake in Agrobanka of "up to 20 percent" but that any stake the EBRD would take would be separate from the majority holding.
Earlier, Klumpar said London-based HSBC Investment Bank would advise on the restructuring of Agrobanka and conduct the selection of new investors.
Klumpar said he expected the search for a strategic investor to be concluded within five months.
He said that the majority stake would either come from a direct sale from existing shareholders or an equity increase to achieve the 51 percent holding.

The central bank put Agrobanka under what it called "temporary forced administration" in Septemeber because of its poor liquidity stemming from a loss of confidence in Agrobanka on the Prague inter-bank money market.

The CNB said the crisis of confidence was due to Agrobanka's connection to a secretive Czech investment group called Motoinvest, and that it would search for a strategic equity partner to replace shareholders connected to Motoinvest.
The crisis came after the August failure of a small Plzen-based bank, Kreditni Banka a.s., which also was connected to Motoinvest.
The exact stakes held by Motoinvest or investors connected to the group, have not been disclosed.
